- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/auth/config (route, a path literal in a comment in PageComponentSchema))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/ui.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93b4acb57ec23c4e94a7047133ce612f89a13838` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `39b30b20b1596ba8db1b3fc1882e50a38fa3e51f` — the merge of head `a150ec532fa85f2502c7c31c1bd0afced7a51b39` into base `93b4acb57ec23c4e94a7047133ce612f89a13838`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 39b30b20b1596ba8db1b3fc1882e50a38fa3e51f && git checkout 39b30b20b1596ba8db1b3fc1882e50a38fa3e51f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 93b4acb57ec23c4e94a7047133ce612f89a13838 a150ec532fa85f2502c7c31c1bd0afced7a51b39 && git checkout -B drift-repro 93b4acb57ec23c4e94a7047133ce612f89a13838 && git merge --no-ff a150ec532fa85f2502c7c31c1bd0afced7a51b39

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93b4acb57ec23c4e94a7047133ce612f89a13838
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 93b4acb57ec23c4e94a7047133ce612f89a13838` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a150ec532fa85f2502c7c31c1bd0afced7a51b39`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/page.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/object-refinement-check-exports.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts, packages/spec/liveness/page.json, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json, .changeset/24265-app-page-record-binding.md, content/docs/ui/pages.mdx, and on main: packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts, packages/spec/src/data/context-tokens.zod.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.ts, docs/adr/0068-unified-user-context-and-built-in-identity-roles.md, docs/adr/0089-unify-visibility-predicate-naming.md; objectui main 32b492b6: packages/app-shell/src/providers/ExpressionProvider.tsx, packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx, packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/recordBinding.tsx

Inputs: card #24265 (body, claim 6246461293, dev report 6247235785), PR #24275 (body, its 16 files, the net diff against main 93b4acb5), and the head's 39 check-runs, read at 2026-10-18T07:54Z. The head had not moved past a150ec5 at that read. The rest of the diff (the generated artifacts, content/docs/references/**, the strictness-ledger counts) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `PageSchema.record` (`PageRecordBindingSchema`, strict `{ object, view?, filter?, sort? }`): one new optional authorable key on `ui/Page` and four keys on the new `ui/PageRecordBinding` shape (`authorable-surface/ui.json`). RIGHT. The shape is `ElementDataSourceSchema` minus `limit`, with the same alias table; `limit`, `id` and `recordId` are refused through `guidance` with a prescription, so an AI that carries the component binding up to the page is refused loudly, never folded. On the key name, which the dev asked this review to judge: `record` equals the root it binds, and the component-level precedent (`dataSource`) is a list binding that happens to take one row for the record blocks, so reusing that name at page level would have carried the many-rows reading the page refuses. The four aliased spellings (`boundRecord`, `recordBinding`, `recordSource`, `dataSource`) fold onto it and collide with no PageSchema key or alias on main. The name stands.
2. No new expression root. RIGHT, and the load-bearing judgment of the card. `record` is already a contract-bound root of the page-component `visibleWhen` (the describe on main) and the runtime root ADR-0089 D1 names; the lint's declared set is `@objectstack/formula` `SCOPE_ROOTS` plus `VIEW_PAGE_EXTRA_ROOTS` (`current_user`, `page`), judged with no page-type derivation, so `record.plan` on an `app` page lints green today and `packages/lint` is correctly untouched. Nothing only the control plane can fill is named: the row is read through the data API every host serves, and the spec's own `{current_org_id}` context token (`data/context-tokens.zod.ts`, resolved on both sides of the wire) lets a binding `filter` select the caller's organisation row, which is what makes the ruled environments page servable from the platform alone.
3. `checkPageRecordBindingPlacement`: the key is refused on every page whose `type` is not `app` (the default is `record`, `PAGE_TYPE_DEFAULT`), with one sentence for a record page and one for a page with no row; exported from `@objectstack/spec/ui`, attached by identifier as the seventh PageSchema check, pinned by six fixtures and the declaration, attachment and barrel-identity counts in `object-refinement-check-exports.test.ts`; the dev's ablation of the accept arm failed exactly the accepting fixture. RIGHT: the rule and its pin land as one change.
4. The `visibleWhen` docblock and describe: `record` is the record a record page opens or the row an app page's binding reads; a block's own `dataSource` binds no `record` for its siblings or for its own gate; a count or a plan is a FIELD on the row, not `features.*`. RIGHT on the cited code: objectui's `configEvaluationScope` binds `record` only from `RecordContext`, and on an `app` page that context is provided only by `BoundRecordScope` around a record block's BODY (`recordBinding.tsx`); `features` is `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES`, deployment-level flags served to anonymous clients by plugin-auth's `getPublicConfig()` under a key-set drift guard. The ambient-roots paragraph (`features`, `os.user`: renderer behaviour, not contract) is unchanged. One reading note, not a defect: the describe's "never `features.*`" is scoped to a plan; `features.X` remains the right root for the auth-capability gates that `requiresFeature` lowers to.
5. Public exports `PageRecordBindingSchema`, `PageRecordBinding`, `PageRecordBindingParsed` and `checkPageRecordBindingPlacement` (`api-surface`, `export-origins`, `declaration-map`), and the new published JSON schema `ui/PageRecordBinding` (`json-schema.manifest`). RIGHT, all additive.
6. `dropped-refinements.baseline.json`: one more schema and one more site (`ui/PageRecordBinding` at `filter.element`), and `ui/Page`'s first `ViewFilterRule` site moving from `interfaceConfig.filterBy.element` to `record.filter.element`. RIGHT: no new refinement pattern is admitted; it is `ViewFilterRuleSchema`'s existing rule reached through one more path, the same class as every other `filter.element` row, and the move is declaration order inside PageSchema.
7. Liveness: `record` and its six leaves `planned`, evidence at the parse refusal and the shape; `state-counts/page.md` planned 0 to 7; the metadata-admin form ledger gains an `omit` row for `record` on the `print` precedent. RIGHT as a grading: the parse half is live, the renderer half is the card's own sequencing (objectui#12931 is `pm:blocked` on this card), the same posture as `ElementApiDataSourceSchema`. See ③ F2 for the note's missing pointer.
8. Declaring `PageRecordBindingSchema` after `PageComponentSchema` so `skills/objectstack-ui/references/_index.md` stays byte-identical. RIGHT, and not a dodge: `exportListDescription` names the first five authorable exports in source order, so declared earlier the new schema would have displaced `PageComponentSchema` from that line, a worse index bought with a governed-path edit.
9. ADR-0068 D1 and ADR-0089 (the two prior decisions the claim named): neither is contradicted. ADR-0068 rules the user object only and its Non-goals fence `record` / `org` / `env` out; ADR-0089 D1 is the root this reuses, and its fail-open-at-render posture is what the "a faulting predicate renders the component" sentences restate.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/24265-app-page-record-binding.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **minor**, body opening `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, identical to the PR body's line. MATCHES what the diff publishes: one new optional authorable key and shape, four exports, one JSON schema file, four aliases; nothing removed, renamed or narrowed, and every existing page parses as before (the only new refusal fires on a key that did not exist). No ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed (not breaking). `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations, each answered:
- D1 (`test:repo` run though not owed): no effect on the contract; noted.
- D2 (the liveness row drilled to its leaves instead of growing the undrilled-containers baseline; the dropped-refinements move): both the right direction, judged in ① 6 and 7.
- D3 (the primary checkout detached to check the claim's branch out in a worktree): the dev's own container, and the branch sat at `origin/main` `a422f04fe`, so no shared-tree hazard was realised. Noted.

`open_questions` (the card's three questions, delegated by the card to the seat and by the seat to the dev's measurement):
- Q1, the root for an `app` page's bound row. ANSWERED: A, the existing `record` bound by `PageSchema.record`, is right on all four axes (business need, long-term soundness, AI-error-proofing, startup focus): it serves the ruled pull directly, reuses ADR-0089 D1's root and the record blocks' one-row semantics, is strict and refused off `app` pages, and adds no root for the lint, the formula engine or the editor to learn. B would have given `PageVariable.source` a second meaning; C a third row spelling. The key-name question is judged in ① 1.
- Q2, the tier without a cloud-only root. ANSWERED: A, a field on the bound row (`record.plan`). `features` cannot carry it: `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES` is a closed, deployment-level, anonymous registry whose served key set is drift-guarded against `getPublicConfig()`, so a per-organisation plan there is exactly the control-plane-only fill the card forbids. Promoting `features` to contract-bound stays undecided, as the dev wrote; nothing here needs it.
- Q3, the count. ANSWERED: A, a `summary` roll-up on the bound row read as `record.FIELD`; no root and no evaluator capability. A hand-off, not an escalation: the data half is the app's. The control plane's organisation object needs the roll-up and its plan field, and its environments page becomes a `type: 'app'` page carrying the binding (a `{current_org_id}` filter selects the caller's organisation). The card's Order names only objectui#12931; the cloud-side card is for the seat to route under the cross-repo rule. This review cannot read that repository.

Flags of my own:
- F1 (`content/docs/ui/pages.mdx`, the lane seat's ACCEPT): the `visibleWhen` cell this PR REWRITES still ends "Legacy alias `visibility` is accepted but deprecated per ADR-0089", false since 18, where `visibility` is a `retiredKey()` tombstone on the very schema this PR edits. The dev lists it as pre-existing drift; a sentence re-asserted in a rewritten cell is not pre-existing. One parenthetical deletion on the next push. The Zod text is the contract and is correct, so this does not move the verdict.
- F2 (`packages/spec/liveness/page.json`, row `record`): the planned note names the measurement and the flip condition but not the consumer card. The precedent planned rows (`settledWhen`, `conditionalFormatting` in `liveness/field.json`) name theirs; add objectui#12931 to the note on the next push, or when the row flips to `live`.
- F3 (the check-runs on this head, at the reading above): `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Build Docs`, every `Lint ·` lane and `Type Check · source gates` were `success`; `Test Core (1 to 6 of 6)`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates` and `Type Check · debt ledger` were still `in_progress`. The contract verdict below is this review's; those conclusions are theirs, and the landing waits for all of them (the generated-artifact gates live in the type-check job).
- No escalation: no axis conflict, and no prior ruling or ADR answers any of the three questions differently.
